sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: I have docked below at Interactive Lab 1: the Nyquist Sampling, Spectral Aliasing, and ADC Quantization Studio! Select the Critical Aliasing preset above to watch a thirty-two hundred hertz physical wave fold into a phantom eight hundred hertz alias when sampled at four thousand hertz, and adjust the ADC slider to inspect quantization error across eight, twelve, and sixteen-bit tiers!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look at those dual canvases directly above! In the left canvas, sampling below Nyquist produces that red dashed phantom wave, while on the right, eight-bit quantization turns our smooth sine wave into a jagged staircase with twelve millivolts of error noise!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: I have docked below at Interactive Lab 2: the Constrained Telemetry Overhead and Battery Longevity Studio! Switch between the Five-Year Environmental Probe and Continuous Cloud Streamer presets above to see how ninety-five percent deadband suppression cuts time-averaged current down to forty-five microamps, leaping battery life from less than two days to over five years!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Watch that battery curve on the right canvas! When you drag the deadband suppression slider past ninety percent, the curve rockets upward like a hockey stick, proving why local edge filtering is essential for remote sensors!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 1! For an industrial acoustic emission sensor monitoring pump bearing wear up to fourteen kilohertz, calculate the absolute minimum theoretical sampling frequency and identify the required analog filtering stage.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Checkpoint time, Dr. Nova! We have fourteen kilohertz defect frequencies on a high-speed pump. Which option guarantees clean digitization without spectral aliasing?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Spot on! By the Nyquist criterion, the sampling frequency must satisfy f s greater than or equal to two times f max, or at least twenty-eight kilohertz—with forty-eight kilohertz common in practice! Furthermore, an analog anti-aliasing low-pass filter must precede the ADC to eliminate out-of-band harmonics before sampling.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. Remember that the Nyquist criterion requires sampling at least twice the maximum frequency, so fourteen kilohertz requires at least twenty-eight kilohertz! Furthermore, digital software filtering cannot remove aliases once sampled; an analog filter must precede the ADC.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 2! Calculate the quantization step size delta in millivolts and the theoretical SQNR in decibels for a twelve-bit ADC operating over a three point three volt full-scale span.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Let's check the ADC math on Slide 11! Twelve bits and three point three volts full scale. What is the step size and theoretical signal-to-noise ratio?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Correct! Three point three volts divided by forty-ninety-six levels yields zero point eight zero six millivolts, and six point zero two times twelve plus one point seven six yields seventy-four point zero one decibels of dynamic fidelity!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. Divide three point three volts by two to the twelfth, which is forty-ninety-six, giving zero point eight zero six millivolts. Then apply the theoretical SQNR formula: six point zero two times twelve plus one point seven six yields seventy-four point zero one decibels.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 3! Given a twenty-four hundred milliamp-hour battery with usable capacity of twenty-forty milliamp-hours, active current of forty-five milliamps for one second per minute, and sleep current of eight microamps, compare baseline periodic lifespan against ninety-five percent deadband suppression.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Final checkpoint, Dr. Nova! In our battery model, how dramatically does ninety-five percent deadband edge suppression extend the operating life of an environmental node?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Outstanding mastery! At one second per minute, the duty cycle yields an average current of zero point seven five seven nine milliamps and one hundred twelve point two days of life. Suppressing ninety-five percent of redundant events drops daily active time to seventy-two seconds, surging battery life to five point one two years!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. In the baseline periodic mode, active current dominates, yielding one hundred twelve point two days. With ninety-five percent deadband suppression, the node spends ninety-nine point nine percent of the day in eight-microamp sleep, leaping lifespan past five years!
